$schema_note: UCI-000001 Universal Certification Integrity. This file is the governed EXPECTATION. engine/certification_integrity computes the OBSERVATION and compares. Nothing in the package writes this file: an observation that can rewrite its own expectation is not a measurement, and `make uci-inventory` prints the discovered surface for a human to paste here precisely so that the adoption is a reviewable diff rather than a regeneration.
name: Universal Certification Integrity
authority: NONE — DERIVED TRUTH. This programme legislates nothing, owns no threshold and grants no exemption. It measures whether the coverage denominator equals the executable surface, whether every executable surface is governed, and whether a certification run is attributable to a commit.
principle: A percentage is a ratio, and a ratio is only as honest as its denominator. The repository governed its numerator for years and reported 97.9% of a denominator covering 49.4% of the executable surface. Neither number was wrong; the pair was never compared.

$what_produced_this.measurement: At b51f6f84, over 1,524 tracked non-test Python files carrying 183,310 statements: 905 files are inside the coverage denominator and 619 are not. Executable-surface coverage, computed for the first time, was 44.9% against a reported 97.9%.

unmeasured_surface.00-MASTER/*/*_engine.py: 39 files, 20,359 statements — every one an enforcement artifact UEC-000001 governs by name
unmeasured_surface.intelligence/: 65 files, 5,565 statements — in pytest testpaths, in no --cov flag
unmeasured_surface.engine/recursive_knowledge: 16 files, 2,849 statements — an implicit namespace package, admitted to the denominator at 2ad1efcf

$what_produced_this.false_green_recovered: A coverage.xml produced while two processes wrote the same path contained a COMPLETE, valid document at lines 1-90,556 followed by a second process's content, and ended with a second </coverage>. A consumer reading the first document would have obtained a valid-but-wrong coverage report; a consumer checking the tail would have been reassured by a proper closing tag. Preserved at .uci-evidence/coverage.xml.truncated-by-concurrent-run. This is why every measurement in this programme runs inside a frozen extraction and why the coverage reader refuses a document it cannot parse rather than salvaging one.

$relationship_to_uec: UEC-000001 and UCI-000001 measure overlapping populations with deliberately different strictness, and BOTH figures are reported rather than reconciled. UEC-L-06 counts distinct invoking TEXTS, so an engine named by thirty-three workflow files scores 33. UCI-L-05 counts invocation PLANE TYPES, so the same engine scores 1 for `ci`. UEC measures 15 single-plane artifacts and 18 untested engines; UCI measures 14 and 25 over a population of 48 engines including engine/*/gate.py modules. Neither supersedes the other and neither ratchet is derived from the other: silently overwriting a governed ceiling with a stricter measurement would be an ungoverned adoption event, which Rule 1 forbids.

laws.name: coverage_scope_equals_executable_scope
laws.question: is every executable artifact inside the measured denominator?

laws.name: every_file_has_a_governing_authority
laws.question: does some authority claim every tracked Python artifact?

laws.name: governance_engines_are_measured
laws.question: is every enforcement engine's executed fraction known?

laws.name: every_engine_has_a_test
laws.question: does a test module reference every governance engine?

laws.name: every_engine_has_two_invocation_planes
laws.question: is every engine reachable from at least two plane TYPES?

laws.name: measured_files_have_execution_paths
laws.question: does every substantial measured file expose a callable a test could enter?

laws.name: every_ceiling_binds_a_measurement
laws.question: does every declared ceiling bind a measurement that exists?

$ratchet_semantics: TWO-SIDED, and the lower side is the half that matters. Above the ceiling is new debt and is refused. BELOW the ceiling is ALSO refused: the debt was repaid and the ceiling was not tightened, so the declaration is carrying slack that a future regression can occupy in total silence. The satisfied state is equality, exactly. Rule 1 forbids raising a ceiling without measured justification; this construction additionally forbids leaving one loose, which is how a ratchet decays into decoration. Every value below is a CEILING TO BE DRIVEN TO ZERO, not a budget to be spent.

ratchet.$executable_outside_denominator: TIGHTENED 607 -> 65 at 389ccd91 by admitting the five top-level layers (service, data, application, infrastructure, intelligence) to the denominator, which also wired up 3,995 passing tests that no testpaths entry collected. The remaining 65 are 48 files under 00-MASTER (39 of them the *_engine.py gate engines, tracked separately by unmeasured_governance_engines), 13 under 00-BOOK/tools including ukb.py, and one each under 00-CMG/tools, scripts/, engine/ and platform/. Mandate Rule 2 requires 0. Reducing this further requires admitting 00-MASTER and 00-BOOK/tools, which needs those engines to be importable under test rather than only executable as scripts -- a real change, not a setting.
ratchet.$ungoverned_executables: TIGHTENED 570 -> 27 at 389ccd91. The five admitted layers accounted for 543 of the 570: they were claimed by no coverage scope, no UEC inventory, no frozen-path set and no declared exclusion. The remaining 27 are 00-BOOK/tools (13), 00-MASTER non-engine executables (10) and one each under 00-CMG/tools, scripts/, engine/ and platform/. Rule 3 requires 0.
ratchet.$unmeasured_governance_engines: All 39 of 00-MASTER/*/*_engine.py. Each is an enforcement artifact UEC-000001 governs by name and several are verify.sh certification stages, yet the fraction of each that any test executes is unknown. A gate whose executed fraction is unknown can rot into a no-op and keep reporting OPEN, which is the sharpest false green in the repository. Rule 2 and Rule 5 require 0.
ratchet.$engines_without_tests: 25 of 48 governance engines that no test module references, measured by AST evidence with docstrings excluded (a module that DESCRIBES an engine has not exercised it). Differs from UEC's 18 because the population and the needle rules differ; see $relationship_to_uec. Rule 5 requires 0 and additionally requires direct, behaviour, failure-path, mutation and integration tests for each, which this counter does not yet distinguish.
ratchet.$single_plane_engines: 14 engines reachable from fewer than two invocation PLANE TYPES. Rule 6 requires 0 and prefers 3. Because plane types are coarser than invoking texts, an engine can satisfy UEC-L-06 and fail this: reachable from thirty-three workflows and nothing else is thirty-three texts and one plane, and a repository whose only invoker is CI cannot be verified locally.
ratchet.$files_with_no_execution_path: RAISED 6 -> 10 at 389ccd91, and the justification is measured rather than asserted. The population grew because the DENOMINATOR grew: four of the four new entries (infrastructure/band13_meta.py, infrastructure/governance_meta.py, infrastructure/security_meta.py, service/band11_freeze_meta.py) are declarative constant modules in layers admitted in that same commit. They were always in this state and were previously unmeasured, so this is newly VISIBLE surface, not new debt -- the distinction Rule 1 turns on. All ten entries are package facades or constant modules whose coverage is necessarily import-only; the law's purpose is to DISCLOSE that, so that a reader does not mistake import coverage for exercised behaviour. It is a disclosure ratchet and must not grow silently, which is what the two-sided comparison enforces.

$verification_rules.Rule 7 immutable: Certification runs inside a `git archive <sha>` extraction, sealed into a git repository with author, committer and both dates pinned so the sealing commit's SHA is a pure function of the archived bytes. Verified deterministic across independent extractions. The seal is REQUIRED, not a convenience: the suite cannot be collected from a bare extraction, because engine/execution_environment/discovery.py:79 refuses to resolve a repository root with no git and every gate deriving its population from `git ls-files` faults the same way. The outer repository's HEAD, porcelain digest and tracked-file digest are sampled before and after every run and any difference discards the measurement.
$verification_rules.Rule 8 and 11 reproducibility: N independent runs over one frozen tree, compared as covered-line SETS per file, never as percentages: two runs that executed different lines routinely report the same ratio, so a percentage comparison passes on exactly the divergence being tested for.
$verification_rules.Rule 9 order independence: engine/certification_integrity/pytest_shuffle.py, opt-in twice over (-p AND UCI_SHUFFLE_SEED) so the default order is untouched and UVI-L-08's deterministic sharding contract stays measurable. Verified non-vacuous: a seed genuinely reorders, reproduces across invocations, and is echoed into the run header so a failing permutation is replayable.
$verification_rules.Rule 10 shard equivalence: The shard partition is round-robin over sorted test modules, deliberately NOT the cost-weighted longest-processing-time assignment engine/verification_intelligence/execution.py uses, because an audit that ran the audited code would be a tautology. Statements, covered lines, file count, branches valid and branches covered are each asserted separately rather than taken as implied by line-set equality.

exit_semantics.0: OPEN — every blocking law measured and holds
exit_semantics.1: CLOSED — a blocking law measured and REFUSED
exit_semantics.2: FAULT — no verdict reachable; the declaration or the surface could not be measured
